# fjordrun_service_variables (Resource)

The variables of a service in one environment. Works for functions too.

**References and generated values.** Values may contain `${{Service.VAR}}`, `${{shared.VAR}}` and `${{secret(32)}}`. The state holds what you wrote, not what it resolves to, so a changing reference is no diff. A `${{secret(N)}}` generator is expanded once, when the variable is first written; it stays as written in the configuration and state, and later applies keep the generated value. Read resolved values with the `fjordrun_service_variables` or `fjordrun_shared_variables` data source.

**Exclusive or partial.** With `exclusive = true` (the default) this resource owns all the variables: others, set elsewhere, are removed. With `exclusive = false` it only manages the keys in `variables`, which is what you want on services that came from a template, whose variables include generated passwords.

~> Values are sensitive and kept in Terraform state: use an encrypted remote state backend.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "team_id" {
  type = string
}

resource "fjordrun_project" "shop" {
  team_id = var.team_id
  name    = "shop"
}

resource "fjordrun_service" "web" {
  project_id     = fjordrun_project.shop.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_project.shop.default_environment_id
  name           = "web"
  source         = { type = "image", image = "nginxdemos/hello:0.4" }
}

resource "fjordrun_service_variables" "web" {
  service_id     = fjordrun_service.web.id
  environment_id = fjordrun_service.web.environment_id

  variables = {
    LOG_LEVEL      = "info"
    SESSION_SECRET = "$${{secret(48)}}"            # generated once, then kept
    DATABASE_URL   = "$${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}" # a reference to another service
    APP_ENV        = "$${{shared.APP_ENV}}"        # a reference to a shared variable
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) Environment ID.
- `service_id` (String) Service ID.
- `variables` (Map of String, Sensitive) Variables by name. Names look like `MY_VAR`.

### Optional

- `auto_deploy` (Boolean) Deploy when this resource is created or changes. Leave out to use the provider's `auto_deploy` (default `true`). With `false` the change is saved and goes live with the next deployment, which `fjordrun_deployment` makes explicit.
- `exclusive` (Boolean) Whether this resource owns all the variables (default), or only the keys in `variables`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `service_id/environment_id`.
- `variables_hash` (String, Sensitive) Digest of `variables`, for `fjordrun_deployment` triggers. Sensitive, because it is derived from secret values.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# service_id/environment_id. Variables come in as the API holds them: a generator in your configuration
# shows as a change once, and that apply keeps the generated value.
terraform import fjordrun_service_variables.web 77777777-7777-7777-7777-777777777777/66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666
```
